name: CIG High Plains Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: CIG High Plains Pipeline; WYCO High Plains Pipeline

researcher_notes: Re-checked the roster: no row for this line. P0168 is the whole Colorado Interstate Gas system, P0359 Cheyenne Connector and P0166 Cheyenne Plains are different pipes, so this is not a match. The Colorado Interstate Gas 2008 annual report to the SEC says the 164 mile, 24 and 30 inch High Plains pipeline from the Cheyenne Hub in northeast Colorado to the Fort St. Vrain power plant went into service in November 2008. It is owned by WYCO Development LLC, a 50/50 joint venture of Colorado Interstate Gas and a Public Service Company of Colorado affiliate (Xcel Energy), and is operated by Colorado Interstate Gas. A Natural Gas Intelligence article on the 2007 federal draft environmental statement gives 164 miles, 24 and 30 inch pipe, 900 MMcf/d. The EIA August 2026 projects release (sheet Historical Projects 1996-2024, Excel row 551, project CIG High Plains Project, completed 2008-11-15) lists 216 million dollars, 164 miles, 900 MMcf/d, 24 and 30 inch, FERC docket CP07-207. Cost and capacity come from EIA only (one origin; the cost is unpaired). Pipeline is existing and operating, so the concrete-step test is met by in-service. Length 164 mi is well over the 25 km rule. The 10-K also says WYCO owns a separate state-regulated intrastate piece pipeline and a compressor station, which are not included. Parent left blank: ownership is shared by two companies, so record both as owners if the team wants Colorado Interstate Gas Company LLC and Public Service Company of Colorado as Owner1 and Owner2 at 50 percent each; WYCO is the title holder in the 10-K. Owner spelling: WYCO Development LLC has no exact gazetteer hit (only a fuzzy 'Development' that was not adopted), so it would be a new entity. Route not searched beyond the roster; no route is on file, so RouteType is unavailable pending a routes-repo candidate (the FERC filing for CP07-207 and the EIA-era maps are leads).  The FERC order for docket CP07-207 was not opened.
